metadata.title: AI@UNCW Project Dashboard
metadata.identity: The AI Hub Orchestrates and GAABS Supports AI Builders.
metadata.subidentity: GAABS is the advanced tool-building arm within The AI Hub.
metadata.publicNotice: This public dashboard contains approved summary information only. Project-file-only information is not live-verified.

executiveSummary: The AI Hub and GAABS remain in a foundation-building phase. This update preserves the public status boundaries established in the July 27 reports while no new verified public outcomes are added. The initiative continues to prioritize responsible readiness, practical adoption support, governance, and bounded planning rather than a broad service launch.
priorities: Verify and address any material issue associated with public AI Hub website availability and content
Continue responsible planning for practical ChatGPT EDU use-support materials
Determine whether any educational-agent concept offers clear value beyond maintainable written guidance before committing to build it
Confirm prerequisites, supervision, scope, validation, and continuity planning before beginning any student consulting pilot work
Maintain established governance, review, and publication boundaries

risks.statement: Draft materials could be mistaken for approved policy or broad service availability.
risks.mitigation: Keep draft and review labels visible and publish only through an authorized route.

risks.statement: AI advisory work could be misunderstood as replacing established shared governance.
risks.mitigation: State advisory limits explicitly and recognize existing authorities.

risks.statement: Workshop access, network, pacing, or login issues could disrupt delivery.
risks.mitigation: Test the complete participant path and maintain a safe no-login fallback.

risks.statement: Late-July delivery and institutional-service obligations could exceed available capacity.
risks.mitigation: Protect Institute preparation and delivery windows, sequence new work behind scheduled delivery, and avoid adding commitments without identifying what they displace.

risks.statement: The shared consultation model could be described inaccurately as GAABS-owned or GAABS-only.
risks.mitigation: Use shared-space language that recognizes Library facilitation and the broader consultation role.

risks.statement: The completed EDU-license rollout could be misrepresented as an effectiveness study even though it was not systematic or study-coordinated.
risks.mitigation: Describe available evidence only as descriptive adoption monitoring and require advance coordination before any future prospective evaluation.

risks.statement: Cross-system AI-readiness coordination could be interpreted as a UNCW commitment before scope or authority is clear.
risks.mitigation: Treat the July 22 discussion as exploratory coordination until participants, decision rights, expected contributions, and follow-up are documented.

risks.statement: Website launch content could be mistaken for approved policy or broad service availability.
risks.mitigation: Verify the public launch, preserve review and ownership boundaries, and correct material issues promptly.

risks.statement: A possible educational agent could duplicate static guidance or imply endorsement before its purpose and maintenance model are clear.
risks.mitigation: Establish the article baseline, audience, source ownership, and agent-specific value before committing to build it.

risks.statement: Tool access, centrally managed funding, or student-account readiness could delay the experimental consulting pilot.
risks.mitigation: Confirm all prerequisites before student work begins and retain clear operating controls.

risks.statement: Student turnover could leave an early prototype without a maintainer.
risks.mitigation: Use peer learning, document handoff responsibilities, and name continuity ownership before implementation.

risks.statement: The first pilot could become too technically ambitious for its client need or cohort readiness.
risks.mitigation: Favor maintainable solutions and confirm project scope, source ownership, and validation criteria before implementation.
